intro: «Se me da bien» talks about what you do well or badly: the verb agrees with the skill, not with you.
p.se me da bien.consejo: The subject is the skill: «El inglés se me da bien». Swap «me» for «te» or «le» to change person.
p.se me dan bien.consejo: «Dan» is used when the skill is plural: «las matemáticas se me dan bien».
p.se me da mal.consejo: To say something is not your strong point, «no se me da bien» also works. Stronger: «se me da fatal».
p.a mí.consejo: It is added for contrast: «A mí se me da bien, a ti no». The «me» already says who.
p.los idiomas.consejo: It is masculine even though it ends in -a: «el idioma», «los idiomas». «Lengua» is feminine.
p.las matemáticas.consejo: It is used in the plural: «las matemáticas». The accent mark falls on the third syllable: «ma-te-má-ti-cas».
p.la cocina.consejo: It is also the room of the house where you cook. The context shows the meaning.
p.cantar.consejo: An infinitive used as a subject always takes the singular: «Cantar se me da mal».
p.dibujar.consejo: The «j» sounds like a strong h. It belongs to the family of «dibujo».
p.bastante.consejo: Before an adverb it does not change: «bastante bien». Before a plural noun it does: «bastantes amigos».
p.fatal.consejo: It is colloquial and sounds stronger than «mal»: «Cantar se me da fatal».
p.regular.consejo: In this sense it is an adverb and does not change: «Se me da regular».
b1.texto:
**Se me da bien** (one thing) and **se me dan bien** (several things) talk about your skills. The verb agrees with the skill, not with you:

- **El inglés** se me da bien.
- **Las matemáticas** se me dan bien.
- **Cantar** se me da mal. With an infinitive, the verb is always singular.

To talk about someone else, change **me** to **te**, **le**, **nos**, **os** or **les**. **A mí**, **a ti**… add emphasis or contrast.

You can grade the skill: **muy bien**, **bastante bien**, **regular**, **mal**, **fatal**.
b2.titulo: Getting ready for the neighbourhood party
b2.f7.texto: You make the posters for the party.
b4.texto:
The structure is **se** + pronoun + **da / dan** + **bien / mal**:

- **se me** da / dan: I
- **se te** da / dan: you
- **se le** da / dan: he, she, usted
- **se nos** da / dan: we
- **se os** da / dan: you (vosotros)
- **se les** da / dan: they, ustedes

Use **da** with one thing or with an infinitive, and **dan** with several things. To negate, put **no** before **se**: **No se me da bien** el dibujo.
b4.e1.texto: We are not good at sports.
b5.f0.texto: The neighbourhood square smells of fresh paint and newly baked bread.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía paints the letters of the posters with a fine brush.
b5.f2.texto: Drawing has come easily to her since she was a girl.
b5.f3.texto: Pablo holds the ladder with both hands and looks upwards.
b5.f4.texto: He hums an out-of-tune song while she paints.
b5.f5.texto: The neighbours arrive at midday with trays of hot empanadas.
b5.f7.texto: Her rice with chicken disappears from the plates in a few minutes.
b5.f8.texto: The stage fills with yellow lights when evening falls.
b5.f9.texto: Pablo goes up with a borrowed guitar and sings very softly.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «el dibujo» is singular, so the verb is «da».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Dan» is for several things. Here there is only one: «el dibujo».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Doy» would agree with «yo», but the subject is the skill.
b6.pregunta: The skill is one single thing. Which verb is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Me» says who is good or bad, but it is not the subject.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Correct: the skill is the subject, which is why the verb is singular.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Fatal» says how well it goes; it is not the subject.
b7.pregunta: In «Cantar se me da fatal», what is the subject?
b8.frase: A mí se me dan bien las matemáticas
b9.o0: Las matemáticas se me da bien.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Las matemáticas» is plural: the verb must be «dan».
b9.o1.refuerzo: The verb agrees with the skill, not with «yo».
b9.o2: Las matemáticas se me dan bien.
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I'm bad at singing.»
b11.frase: A Marta se ____ da bien la música.
b11.o0.refuerzo: «Me» is for «yo». Marta is someone else.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «le» is for he, she or usted.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Les» is for several people. Marta is just one.
b11.pregunta: You talk about Marta, one person. Which pronoun is missing?
b12.o0: La cocina se me da regular.
b12.o1: La cocina se me da fatal.
b12.o2: La cocina se me da muy bien.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Muy bien» is the best, not a middle point.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence says «neither well nor badly»?
p.dan.consejo: In «se nos dan bien» it agrees with the plural skill: «los deportes se nos dan bien».
p.haces.consejo: «Hacer» is irregular only in «yo»: «hago». With «tú» it is regular: «haces». The «h» is silent.
p.carteles.consejo: It is the plural of «el cartel». The singular ends in -l, so the plural adds -es.
p.deportes.consejo: It is masculine: «el deporte». «Hacer deporte» means to play or do sport regularly.
p.pintura.consejo: It is also the art of painting: «la pintura» in a museum. The context tells you which.
p.pinta.consejo: It comes from «pintar», a regular verb: «pinto», «pintas», «pinta».
p.pincel.consejo: In Spain the «c» before «e» sounds «th». The plural is «pinceles».
p.fino.consejo: It changes with gender: «fino», «fina». It can also mean refined: «una persona fina».
p.sostiene.consejo: It comes from «sostener», like «tener»: the «e» becomes «ie» in «sostienes», «sostiene».
p.arriba.consejo: The opposite is «abajo». «Hacia arriba» means upwards, and «arriba» alone means up there.
p.tararea.consejo: It comes from «tararear». The «e» and the «a» go in separate syllables: «ta-ra-RE-a».
p.desafinada.consejo: It agrees with «canción»: «desafinada». With a masculine noun: «desafinado».
p.vecinas.consejo: It is the feminine plural of «vecino». The «v» sounds like «b» and the «c» before «i» like «th».
p.bandejas.consejo: The «j» sounds like a strong «h». The singular is «la bandeja».
p.empanadas.consejo: A filled pastry. The shape and the filling change from country to country.
p.calientes.consejo: It is the plural of «caliente». It has no feminine form: «una empanada caliente».
p.maravilla.consejo: «De maravilla» means wonderfully: «se me da de maravilla». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.desaparece.consejo: It comes from «desaparecer». Its yo form is «desaparezco», with «zc», like «aparecer».
p.sube.consejo: It comes from «subir», a regular verb. The opposite is «bajar».
p.prestada.consejo: It comes from «prestar». It agrees with «guitarra»: «prestada». With a masculine noun: «prestado».
p.bajito.consejo: It comes from «bajo» + «-ito». «Hablar bajito» means to speak very softly.
